# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

/**

public enum ClaimStatus {
    DRAFT(null), OPEN("CLAIM_OPENED"), PENDING("CLAIM_PENDING"), SETTLED("CLAIM_SETTLED"), VOID("CLAIM_VOIDED");

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * A grade's rate on a sheet: a percent with two decimals, from a date (null: from the beginning of
 * time) through a date (null: with no end).
 */
public record Rate(String sheetId, String grade, BigDecimal pct, LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {

    /**
     * The grade's rate in force on the date: the one whose from-date is the latest on or before it,
     * unless its to-date is before the date. Empty when the date is before every rate the grade
     * has, or after the to-date of the rate that would apply.
     */
    public static Optional<BigDecimal> inForce(List<Rate> rates, String grade, LocalDate date) {
        return rates.stream()
                .filter((r) -> r.grade().equals(grade))
                .filter((r) -> r.from() == null || !r.from().isAfter(date))
                .max(Comparator.comparing(Rate::from, Comparator.nullsFirst(Comparator.naturalOrder())))
                .filter((r) -> r.to() == null || !r.to().isBefore(date))
                .map(Rate::pct);
    }
}

package net.officefloor.hq.app.rate;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;

/**
 * A grade's rate on a sheet: a percent with two decimals, from a date (null: from the beginning of
 * time) through a date (null: with no end).
 */
public record Rate(String sheetId, String grade, BigDecimal pct, LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {

    /**
     * The grade's rate in force on the date: the one whose from-date is the latest on or before it,
     * unless its to-date is before the date. Empty when the date is before every rate the grade
     * has, or after the to-date of the rate that would apply.
     */
    public static Optional<BigDecimal> inForce(List<Rate> rates, String grade, LocalDate date) {
        return rates.stream()
                .filter((r) -> r.grade().equals(grade))
                .filter((r) -> r.from() == null || !r.from().isAfter(date))
                .max(Comparator.comparing(Rate::from, Comparator.nullsFirst(Comparator.naturalOrder())))
                .filter((r) -> r.to() == null || !r.to().isBefore(date))
                .map(Rate::pct);
    }
}

I made no changes; this was read-only. Each figure the screen shows is worked out **twice**. The browser computes everything you see, mostly in `features/rates/rates.ts`. The server separately computes the same figures for audit lines, settling, statements and period closes, mostly in `claim/ClaimFigure.java`, `rollup/Rollup.java` and `setting/Settings.java`. Names below are the code's own.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Claim row (`claim-*`)
- **claim-number**: given when the claim is opened. It is the sheet's next number. If `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it, the number is counted within the claim's period instead (`<period>-<n>`), or `X-<n>` when it is in no period (`ClaimNumbers.next`). Numbers are never reused, and a voided claim keeps its number.
- **claim-amount / claim-date / claim-note / claim-ref / claim-tags / claim-corrects / claim-opened-by**: stored values. A negative amount is a *correction*: it must name a SETTLED claim of the same person (`ClaimInput`, `CheckCorrection`). Tags are lower-cased, de-duplicated and sorted. `ref` must be unique on the sheet, ignoring case.
- **claim-due** (`claimDue` in the browser, `ClaimFigure.withLate` on the server):
  1. If the claim was settled, it shows the frozen `settledDue`.
  2. Otherwise it starts from the *rate figure*:
     - the `statedDue` when a statement binds it (`isBound`: stated and not PENDING);
     - else amount × the rate of the grade in force **on the claim's date**, using the rate in force on that date (`Rate.inForce`/`rateOn`), ÷100, rounded to 2 places;
     - no rate gives **n/a**.
  3. Then it adds the **late charge**:
     - Only for OPEN or PENDING claims that are not deferred and are not corrections.
     - Days overdue are counted from `overdueFrom`, which is due-by plus the grade's grace days in force on the claim's date.
     - For every full 30 days, it adds the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary date, applied to figure + charge so far. So the charge compounds, and each step is rounded.
     - A statement never binds the late charge.
  4. Then it raises the result to the **floor** in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). Corrections have no floor.
- **Rounding** (`Settings.rounding`/`roundsHalfUp`): half-up if the claim's `roundDate` is before `policyDate`, half-even on or after it. A blank `policyDate` means the sheet's today. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
- **claim-due-by**: fixed when the claim is made. It is the *terms*-th business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays (`businessDaysAfter`).
  - Terms come from the person's own terms, else their grade's terms on that date, else the sheet's terms (default 14) (`termsFor`).
  - It is **kept when the claim is re-dated or edited**.
  - It is re-fixed when a holiday on or before it is added, unless the claim is SETTLED or VOID (`RefixDueBys`).
- **claim-period**: the period containing the **due-by**, not the claim's date.
- **claim-overdue**: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` is before today.
- **claim-deferred / -until**: an OPEN claim with `deferredUntil` after today. While deferred, it counts in no total and gains no late charge.
- **claim-stated**: whether the person's last statement bound this claim.
- **claim-proofs, claim-split-from, claim-late-entry, claim-reminded, claim-batch, claim-log, claim-comments**:
  - `lateEntry` means the claim's due-by fell in a soft-closed period when it was made.
  - A claim can be reminded once per sheet's today, and only while OPEN or PENDING.
  - `batch` is the bulk-settle batch number.
  - Each log line records the due at that moment.

### Person row
- **person-claimed**: the amounts of the claims that *count*, added up. A claim counts (`counts` / `Claim.counts`) if:
  - it is SETTLED; or
  - it is OPEN or PENDING and either a statement binds it, or it is not held. A claim is held when its date is inside one of the person's holds or the person's retirement date has been reached (`heldOn(date, today)` / `liveHolds`);
  - and in either case it is not deferred.
- **person-due-total**: the dues of the counting claims, added up, skipping n/a, then capped at the `cap` in force on today.
  - It is **n/a** when the grade in force today has no rate today and no counting claim is "kept". A claim is kept if it has a settled due, a bound figure, a figure found under a different grade on its date, or a figure dated on or before today.
- **person-excess**: how far the uncapped total is above the cap.
- **person-settled-total / person-open-total**: the same dues split into SETTLED and OPEN+PENDING, before the cap.
- **person-overdue-count / -total**: counting claims that are overdue.
- **person-aged-0-30 / 31-60 / 61**: dues of counting OPEN or PENDING claims, bucketed by days from the claim's date to today. A future-dated claim goes in 0–30.
- **person-active**: has a counting OPEN or PENDING claim dated within the 30 days up to and including today.
- **person-backing**: the dues of the patrons' SETTLED claims dated within the last 90 days.
- **person-period-<name>-due-total**:
  - For a closed period, the frozen `personTotals` value (0.00 for a person added later).
  - Otherwise, the dues of claims whose due-by is inside the period and that counted at the period's end. Their status at that point comes from the claim log (`countedOn`/`countsAsOf`); holds, deferral and binding are taken as they are now.
- **person-statement-count / stated-total / statement-date**, from `TakeStatement`:
  - The due-total at the moment of the statement (same n/a and cap rules).
  - Every counting claim is bound to its rate figure. A settled claim is bound to its settled due. The late charge and the floor are never bound.
  - Every non-counting claim is unbound.
  - "As of" a date replays rates, settings, grades, holds, statuses and bindings as they stood on that date.
  - `CancelStatement` unbinds everything and does **not** restore any earlier binding.
- **person-grade**: the grade in force on today (`gradeOn`); a person's grades are dated. **person-retired / -from**, **person-terms**, **person-contact**.

### Sheet totals
- **rollup-claimed-total**: all counting amounts.
- **rollup-due-total / rollup-overdue-total / header-due-total / header-overdue-total**: per-person figures added up, skipping n/a. With 3 or more people, the **single highest and single lowest are dropped** (`trimmedSumDue`/`trimmed`).
- **rollup-settled-total / rollup-open-total**: plain sums, not trimmed.
- **rollup-overdue-count**.
- **tag-<t>-due-total**: a claim with two tags counts under both.
- **month-<yyyy-mm>-due-total**.
- **period-due-total**: the frozen `closedTotal` if closed, else the live sum.
- **period-closed**: shows `yes`, `soft` or `no`.
- **summary-grade-X-count / -due-total / -active**: these **leave out retired people**, while `header-people-count` includes them.
- **summary-status-*-count**, **summary-void-<reason>-count**, **header-claims-*-count**.
- **rate-preview-count / -diff**: OPEN or PENDING unbound claims of that grade whose due would change if the candidate rate applied on every date.
- **setting-*-current**: the value in force on today.

### Freezing
- **Settle** freezes the due: rate figure (or the stated figure) + late charge as of today, then the floor applied last. With no rate, nothing is frozen and the due stays live.
- **Approve** freezes the live figure + late charge at that moment.
- **Re-settle** (steward only) freezes it again at the live figure as if OPEN.
- **Statement** freezes the rate figure only.
- **Close / soft-close** freezes `closedTotal` and each person's total. Reopen discards them.

### Who may do what
- **Roles.** A **viewer**, or anyone on an **archived** sheet, can change nothing (`CheckCanChange`). Bulk actions refuse every item instead of throwing.
  - A user with no assigned role is a clerk.
  - A user covered by a delegation for today acts as a steward. Only a steward *by their own assigned role* may delegate.
- **Matrix-controlled actions.** The `perms` matrix decides `open`, `settle`, `void`, `reassign`, `close` (which also covers soft-close) and `reopen`.
  - The standing rule when an entry is blank: open, settle, void and close by clerk or steward; reassign and reopen by steward only.
  - Split uses the `open` permission.
- **Hard-coded steward only, ignoring the matrix:** approve, reject, re-settle, re-date, cancel statement, archive, and voiding a SETTLED claim. The last is also limited to **7 days** after its SETTLED log date.
- **Separation of duties.** Whoever opened or last edited a claim may not settle or approve it (`isOwnedBy`).
- **Clerk limit.** A **clerk** settling a claim whose due is above the clerk limit in force on today sends it to PENDING instead. n/a counts as within any limit.
- **Proof threshold.** A due above the proof threshold (the grade's own, else the sheet's, on the claim's date) with 0 proofs cannot be settled or approved.
- **Note threshold.** A due above the note threshold with an empty note cannot be opened.
- **No role check at all, beyond the viewer/archived check:** settings, rates, roles, today, holidays, periods. A clerk can make themselves steward.

### Statuses and dates
- **Status flow:** DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED, or OPEN → PENDING → SETTLED / back to OPEN. VOID is final. Only a DRAFT can be edited, and only by the user who holds its editor lock for today.
- **Dates:**
  - A blank claim date takes `entryDate` if set, else today (`entryDay`). But **editing** a draft with a blank date uses today, not `entryDate` (`ApplyClaim`).
  - A claim dated **after** the retirement date is refused (`retiredBefore`). From the retirement date on (`retiredOn`), unbound OPEN and PENDING claims stop counting.
  - A hold covers from its from-date to its optional to-date, both inclusive.
  - Setting today closes every open period whose to-date + `graceDays` is before the new today (`AutoClosePeriods`). It also writes SNAPSHOT lines first.
- **Closed period** (`CheckClaimPeriod`, keyed on the claim's **due-by**): blocks edit, open, settle, void, approve, reject, re-settle, defer, split, reassign, proof, lock, and adding a claim. It does **not** block remind or comment. Re-dating into a closed period is allowed, because the due-by doesn't change.
